sentences.zh: 李乂李乂，本名尚真，趙州房子人也。

translations.literal: Li Yi—Li Yi, original name Shangzhen, was a native of Fangzi in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yi, whose original name was Shangzhen, came from Fangzi in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少與兄尚一、尚貞俱以文章見稱，舉進士。

translations.literal: In youth he and his elder brothers Shangyi and Shangzhen were alike famed for literary talent, and all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he and his elder brothers Shangyi and Shangzhen were all renowned for their writing, and each passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong period he rose through several posts to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 時中宗遣使江南分道贖生，以所在官物充直。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Zhongzong sent envoys to the Jiangnan region by separate routes to ransom living creatures, using local government goods to pay the price.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Zhongzong dispatched envoys to the south by separate routes to buy back captive animals, paying with government goods found in each locality.

sentences.zh: 乂上疏曰：「江南水鄉，采捕為業，魚鱉之利，黎元所資，土地使然，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Yi submitted a memorial saying: "The Jiangnan region is a land of rivers and lakes; gathering and catching are its livelihood. The profit of fish and turtles is what the common people rely on—this is how the land is, and it has been so from old.
translations.idiomatic: Yi submitted a memorial, saying: "The Jiangnan region is a country of rivers and lakes where people live by gathering and fishing. Fish and turtles are what the common folk depend on; the land has made it so, and this has long been the case.

sentences.zh: 伏以聖慈含育，恩周動植，布天下之大德，及鱗介之微品。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your sagely compassion embraces and nurtures all things, extending grace to moving creatures and plants alike, spreading great virtue throughout the realm even to the smallest of scaly creatures.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect that Your Majesty's compassionate nurture embraces all living things, extending grace to every creature that moves or grows, and spreading great virtue across the realm even to the lowliest fish and shellfish.

sentences.zh: 雖雲雨之私，有霑於末類；

translations.literal: Though the private favor of cloud and rain may reach the lowest kinds of beings,
translations.idiomatic: Though the private blessing of rain may reach even the humblest creatures,

sentences.zh: 而生成之惠，未洽於平人。

translations.literal: the grace that sustains life has not yet suffused the common people.
translations.idiomatic: the grace that sustains life has not yet reached the common people.

sentences.zh: 何則？

translations.literal: Why is this?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this?

sentences.zh: 江湖之饒，生育無限；

translations.literal: The abundance of rivers and lakes breeds without limit;
translations.idiomatic: The rivers and lakes teem with life beyond counting;

sentences.zh: 府庫之用，支供易殫。

translations.literal: the uses of the treasury are easily exhausted in supporting expenditures.
translations.idiomatic: yet the treasury's resources are soon spent in paying for them.

sentences.zh: 費之若少，則所濟何成；

translations.literal: If the expense is slight, what can be accomplished in relief?
translations.idiomatic: If the expense is small, little can actually be saved;

sentences.zh: 用之倘多，則常支有闕。

translations.literal: If the expenditure is great, the regular budget will fall short.
translations.idiomatic: if it is large, the ordinary budget will fall short.

sentences.zh: 在於拯物，豈若憂人。

translations.literal: When it comes to saving creatures, how can that compare with caring for people?
translations.idiomatic: When the aim is to rescue creatures, how does that compare with relieving the distress of people?

sentences.zh: 且鬻生之徒，唯利斯視，錢刀日至，網罟年滋，施之一朝，營之百倍，未若回救贖之錢物，減困貧之徭賦，活國愛人，其福勝彼。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who sell living creatures look only to profit. Coin and blade increase day by day, nets and traps multiply year by year. What is given in a single morning yields a hundredfold in trade. Better to turn back the funds used for ransom, reduce corvée and taxes on the poor and distressed, revive the state and cherish the people—the blessing would surpass that.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, those who traffic in living creatures care only for profit. Money changes hands daily, and nets and traps multiply year by year. What is spent in a single day returns a hundredfold to their trade. Far better to redirect the funds used for ransom, lighten the corvée and taxes borne by the poor, and revive the state while caring for the people—the blessing would far exceed that.

sentences.zh: 乂知制誥凡數載。

translations.literal: Yi served as drafter of edicts and ordinances for several years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yi drafted edicts and ordinances for several years.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年，遷吏部侍郎，與宋璟、盧從願同時典選，銓敘平允，甚為當時所稱。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingyun he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel; together with Song Jing and Lu Congyuan he then managed selection at the same time. His assessments were fair and even, and he was greatly praised in his day.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jingyun era he was promoted to Vice Minister of Personnel. He served concurrently with Song Jing and Lu Congyuan as overseer of appointments, and his evaluations were so even-handed that contemporaries spoke highly of him.

sentences.zh: 尋轉黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 時睿宗令造金仙、玉真二觀，乂頻上疏諫，帝每優容之。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Ruizong ordered the construction of the Jinxian and Yuzhen monasteries. Yi repeatedly submitted memorials remonstrating, and the emperor each time treated him with gracious forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong ordered the construction of the Jinxian and Yuzhen monasteries, Yi repeatedly submitted memorials in protest, and each time the emperor received him with gracious forbearance.

sentences.zh: 開元初，特令乂與中書侍郎蘇颋纂集起居註，錄其嘉謨昌言可體國經遠者，別編奏之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he was specially ordered, together with Vice Minister of the Secretariat Su Ting, to compile the Diaries of Activity and Repose, recording excellent counsels and splendid words that could embody the state and guide it far, and to submit them separately in compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign he was specially ordered, together with Vice Minister of the Secretariat Su Ting, to compile the court diaries and to select from them excellent counsels and far-sighted words fit to guide the state, which they then submitted in a separate compilation.

sentences.zh: 乂在門下，多所駁正。

translations.literal: While Yi was at the Gate Department, he rejected and corrected many items.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at the Gate Department, Yi rejected and corrected many drafts.

sentences.zh: 開元初，姚崇為紫微令，薦乂為紫微侍郎，外托薦賢，其實引在己下，去其糾駁之權也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan Yao Chong was Director of the Purple Forbidden Office and recommended Yi as Vice Director. Outwardly he claimed to be promoting the worthy; in truth he drew Yi beneath himself and removed his power to criticize and reject.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, Yao Chong was Director of the Purple Forbidden Office and recommended Yi as Vice Director. Outwardly he claimed to be promoting talent; in truth he placed Yi beneath himself and stripped him of his power to criticize and reject drafts.

sentences.zh: 俄拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 乂方雅有學識，朝廷稱其有宰相之望，會病卒。

translations.literal: Yi was refined, elegant, and learned; the court said he had the makings of a chief minister, but he happened to die of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was refined, learned, and accomplished, and the court regarded him as a man with the makings of a chief minister, but he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 兄尚一，清源尉，早卒；

translations.literal: His elder brother Shangyi was magistrate of Qingyuan and died early;
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shangyi, magistrate of Qingyuan, died young;

sentences.zh: 尚貞，官至博州刺史。

translations.literal: Shangzhen rose in office to Prefect of Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhen rose to serve as prefect of Bo.

sentences.zh: 兄弟同為一集，號曰《李氏花萼集》，總二十卷。

translations.literal: The brothers together compiled one collection, entitled Collected Writings of the Li Family at the Flower Calyx, twenty scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers jointly compiled a collection entitled Collected Writings of the Li Family at the Flower Calyx, twenty scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 薛登薛登，本名謙光，常州義興人也。

translations.literal: Xue Deng—Xue Deng, original name Qianguang, was a native of Yixing in Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Deng, whose original name was Qianguang, came from Yixing in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父士通，大業中為鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: His father Shitong served in the Daye era as General of Soaring Hawks.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shitong served during the Daye reign as General of Soaring Hawks.

sentences.zh: 江都之亂，士通與鄉人聞人嗣安等同據本郡，以禦寇賊。

translations.literal: During the turmoil at Jiangdu, Shitong together with his fellow townsman Wenren Sian and others jointly held their home commandery to repel bandits and rebels.
translations.idiomatic: During the upheaval at Jiangdu, Shitong joined his fellow townsman Wenren Sian and others in holding their home commandery against bandits and rebels.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，遣使歸國，高祖嘉之，降璽書勞勉，拜東武州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude he sent an envoy to return to allegiance with the state. Emperor Gaozu praised this and issued an imperial letter of commendation and encouragement, appointing him Prefect of Dongwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wude he sent envoys to submit to the new dynasty. Emperor Gaozu commended him, issued an imperial letter of encouragement, and appointed him prefect of Dongwu.

sentences.zh: 俄而輔公祏於江都構逆，遣其將西門君儀等寇常州，士通率兵拒戰，大破之，君儀等僅以身免。

translations.literal: Before long Fu Gongshi raised rebellion at Jiangdu and sent his generals Ximen Junyi and others to raid Chang Prefecture. Shitong led troops to resist and inflicted a great defeat; Junyi and the others barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fu Gongshi rebelled at Jiangdu and sent his generals Ximen Junyi and others to attack Chang Prefecture. Shitong led troops against them, won a great victory, and Junyi and his men barely escaped with their lives.

sentences.zh: 及公祏平，累功封臨汾侯。

translations.literal: When Gongshi was pacified, he accumulated merit and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Linfen.
translations.idiomatic: After Gongshi was suppressed, Shitong's accumulated merit earned him the title Marquis of Linfen.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷遷泉州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was transferred through several posts to Prefect of Quan and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he rose through several posts to prefect of Quan, where he died.

sentences.zh: 謙光博涉文史，每與人談論前代故事，必廣引證驗，有如目擊。

translations.literal: Qianguang was broadly versed in literature and history. Whenever he discussed stories of former ages with others, he always cited extensive proofs and verification, as though he had seen them with his own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Qianguang was widely versed in literature and history. Whenever he discussed events of earlier ages, he cited extensive evidence with the vividness of an eyewitness.

sentences.zh: 少與徐堅、劉子玄齊名友善。

translations.literal: In youth he was famed on equal terms with Xu Jian and Liu Zixuan and was friendly with them.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was ranked alongside Xu Jian and Liu Zixuan and was close friends with both.

sentences.zh: 文明中，解褐閬中主簿。

translations.literal: In the Wenming era he doffed commoner's garb and became Registrar of Langzhong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wenming reign he entered office as registrar of Langzhong.

sentences.zh: 天授中，為左補闕，時選舉頗濫，謙光上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the Tianshou era he served as Left Remonstrator. At that time appointments were quite lax, and Qianguang submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianshou reign he served as Left Remonstrator. Appointments at the time were notoriously lax, and Qianguang submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 尋轉水部員外郎，累遷給事中、檢校常州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works for Water Control, and through successive promotions became Supervising Censor and Acting Prefect of Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works for Water Control, and eventually rose to Supervising Censor and acting prefect of Chang.

sentences.zh: 屬宣州狂寇硃大目作亂，百姓奔走，謙光嚴備安輯，闔境肅然。

translations.literal: It happened that the reckless bandit Zhu Damu of Xuan Prefecture raised rebellion; the common people fled in panic. Qianguang made strict preparations to settle and pacify the region, and the whole jurisdiction became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel Zhu Damu of Xuan Prefecture rose in revolt and the people fled in panic, Qianguang made strict preparations to restore order, and the whole jurisdiction became calm.

sentences.zh: 轉刑部侍郎，加銀青光祿大夫，再遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice, given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, and again promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Justice, granted the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, and later promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，擢拜御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the Jingyun era he was promoted and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun period he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時僧惠範恃太平公主權勢，逼奪百姓店肆，州縣不能理。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Huifan relied on the power of Princess Taiping and forced the seizure of shops belonging to common people; the prefectures and counties could not deal with it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the monk Huifan, relying on Princess Taiping's power, seized shops from common people by force, and local officials could do nothing about it.

sentences.zh: 謙光將加彈奏，或請寢之，謙光曰：「憲臺理冤滯，何所回避，朝彈暮黜，亦可矣。

translations.literal: Qianguang was about to impeach him, and some asked that the matter be dropped. Qianguang said: "The Censorate exists to settle wrongs and delays—what is there to avoid? To be impeached in the morning and dismissed in the evening would also be acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Qianguang was about to impeach him, and some urged him to let the matter drop. Qianguang said, "The Censorate exists to redress injustice—what is there to avoid? To be impeached in the morning and dismissed by evening would be reward enough."

sentences.zh: 」遂與殿中慕容玽奏彈之，反為太平公主所構，出為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: " He then joined with Palace Censor Murong Ting in submitting an impeachment, but in turn was framed by Princess Taiping and sent out as Prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: " He then joined Palace Censor Murong Ting in impeaching Huifan, but was in turn framed by Princess Taiping and sent out as prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 惠範既誅，遷太子賓客，轉刑部尚書，加金紫光祿大夫、昭文館學士。

translations.literal: After Huifan was executed, he was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then Minister of Justice, with the additional titles of Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Gold Seal and Scholar of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After Huifan was executed, he was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then Minister of Justice, with the additional titles Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Gold Seal and Scholar of the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為東都留守，又轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he served as Defender of the Eastern Capital, then was again transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan he served as defender of the eastern capital, then again as Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 以與太子同名，表請行字，特敕賜名登。

translations.literal: Because he shared the heir apparent's personal name, he submitted a memorial requesting to use his style name, and was specially ordered by edict to be given the name Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Because he shared the heir apparent's personal name, he petitioned to use his style name instead, and an edict specially granted him the name Deng.

sentences.zh: 尋以孽子悅千牛為憲司所劾，放歸田裏。

translations.literal: Before long, because his illegitimate son Yue, a Thousand-Ox Guard, was impeached by the censorate, he was dismissed and sent back to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his illegitimate son Yue, a member of the Thousand-Ox Guard, was impeached by the censorate, and Deng was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其家貧，又特給致仕祿。

translations.literal: The court, because his family was poor, also specially granted him retirement stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Because his family was poor, the court also specially granted him a retirement stipend.

sentences.zh: 七年卒，年七十三，贈晉州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died at the age of seventy-three and was posthumously given the post of Prefect of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year at the age of seventy-three and was posthumously appointed prefect of Jin.

sentences.zh: 撰《四時記》二十卷。

translations.literal: He compiled Records of the Four Seasons in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled Records of the Four Seasons in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 韋湊韋湊，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Cou—Wei Cou was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Cou came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖瓚，隋尚書右丞。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Zan was Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Zan served the Sui as Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 祖叔諧，蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shuxie was Prefect of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shuxie served as prefect of Pu.

sentences.zh: 父玄，桂州都督府長史。

translations.literal: His father Xuan was Chief Administrator of the Guizhou Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xuan was chief administrator of the Guizhou area command.

sentences.zh: 湊，永淳二年，解褐授婺州參軍，累轉揚府法曹參軍。

translations.literal: Cou, in the second year of Yongchun, doffed commoner's garb and was appointed Military Aide of Wu; through successive transfers he became Legal Aide of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cou entered office in the second year of Yongchun as military aide of Wu Prefecture and eventually rose to legal aide of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州人前仁壽令孟神爽豪縱，數犯法，交通貴戚，前後官吏莫敢繩按，湊白長史張潛，請因事除之。

translations.literal: A former magistrate of Renshou named Meng Shenshuang in the prefecture was overbearing and unrestrained, repeatedly violated the law, and had dealings with noble kin. Officials before and after dared not investigate and punish him. Cou reported to Chief Administrator Zhang Qian and asked to remove him by taking advantage of some affair.
translations.idiomatic: A former magistrate of Renshou named Meng Shenshuang in the prefecture was arrogant and lawless, repeatedly broke the law, and cultivated connections with powerful families. Successive officials dared not prosecute him. Cou reported to chief administrator Zhang Qian and asked to remove him when opportunity offered.

sentences.zh: 會神爽坐事推問，湊無所假借，神爽妄稱有密旨，究問引虛，遂杖殺之，遠近稱伏。

translations.literal: It happened that Shenshuang was implicated in an affair and put to interrogation. Cou showed him no indulgence. Shenshuang falsely claimed there was a secret edict; investigation proved the claim empty, and he was beaten to death. Near and far praised and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenshuang was implicated in a case and interrogated, Cou showed him no leniency. Shenshuang falsely claimed a secret edict protected him, but investigation proved the claim false, and he was beaten to death. People near and far applauded the result.

sentences.zh: 湊，景龍中歷遷將作少匠、司農少卿。

translations.literal: Cou, in the Jinglong era, was transferred through several posts to Vice Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings and Vice Minister of the Directorate of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong period Cou rose through several posts to Vice Director of the Directorate for Palace Buildings and Vice Minister of the Directorate of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 嘗以公事忤宗楚客，出為貝州刺史。

translations.literal: Once, on account of official business, he offended Zong Chuke and was sent out as Prefect of Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Once, on official business, he offended Zong Chuke and was sent out as prefect of Bei.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，拜鴻臚少卿，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Cou was appointed Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception and given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, Cou was appointed Vice Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception and granted the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 景雲二年，轉太府少卿，又兼通事舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyun he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and also served concurrently as Imperial Protocol Officer.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingyun he was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury and also served concurrently as imperial protocol officer.

sentences.zh: 時改葬節湣太子，優詔加謚；

translations.literal: At that time the Jiemin Crown Prince was being reburied, and a gracious edict added a posthumous title;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Jiemin Crown Prince was being reburied, and a gracious edict added a posthumous title;

sentences.zh: 又雪李多祚等罪，還其官爵，仍議更加贈官。

translations.literal: the crimes of Li Duozuo and others were also cleared, their offices and titles restored, and there was still discussion of further adding posthumous offices.
translations.idiomatic: the crimes of Li Duozuo and others were also cleared, their offices and titles restored, and officials still debated granting them further posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 湊上書曰：

translations.literal: Cou submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Cou submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 書奏，睿宗引湊謂曰：「誠如卿言。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Ruizong summoned Cou and said: "It is truly as you say.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Ruizong summoned Cou and said, "What you say is true.

sentences.zh: 事已如此，如何改動？

translations.literal: Matters have already come to this—how can they be changed?"
translations.idiomatic: But matters have already gone this far—how can they be changed?"

sentences.zh: 」湊曰：「太子實行悖逆，不可褒美，請稱其行，改謚以一字。

translations.literal: " Cou said: "The crown prince in truth acted in rebellion and must not be praised. I ask that his conduct be described and the posthumous title changed by a single character.
translations.idiomatic: " Cou said, "The crown prince truly acted in rebellion and must not be praised. Describe his conduct and change the posthumous title by a single character.

sentences.zh: 多祚等以兵犯君，非曰無罪，只可雲放，不可稱雪。

translations.literal: Duozuo and others took up arms against their ruler—it cannot be said they were without guilt. One may only say they were released; one cannot call it clearing their crimes."
translations.idiomatic: Duozuo and others took up arms against their ruler—they were not without guilt. Say only that they were released; do not call it clearing their crimes."

sentences.zh: 」帝然其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his words.

sentences.zh: 當時執政以制令已行，難於改易，唯多祚等停贈官而已。

translations.literal: The men then in power held that the ordinance had already been issued and was hard to change; only the additional posthumous offices for Duozuo and the others were stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Those then in power held that the ordinance had already been issued and was hard to change; only the additional posthumous offices for Duozuo and his associates were halted.

sentences.zh: 明年春，起金仙、玉真兩觀，用工巨億。

translations.literal: The next spring construction was begun on the Jinxian and Yuzhen monasteries, using labor on the order of hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring work began on the Jinxian and Yuzhen monasteries at a cost of hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 湊進諫曰：「陛下去夏，以妨農停兩觀作，今正農月，翻欲興功。

translations.literal: Cou advanced a remonstrance saying: "Your Majesty last summer halted work on the two monasteries because it interfered with farming. Now, right in the farming month, you wish instead to undertake construction.
translations.idiomatic: Cou remonstrated, saying, "Your Majesty halted work on the two monasteries last summer because it interfered with farming. Now, in the very heart of the farming season, you wish to resume construction.

sentences.zh: 雖知用公主錢，不出庫物，但土木作起，高價雇人，三輔農人，趨目前之利，舍農受雇，棄本逐末。

translations.literal: Although it is known that the princess's money is used and nothing comes from the treasury stores, once earthworks and timber work begin, men are hired at high wages. Farmers of the Three Adjuncts, chasing immediate profit, abandon farming to accept hire, forsaking the root and pursuing the branch.
translations.idiomatic: Although the princess's funds are used and nothing is drawn from the treasury, once earthworks and timber construction begin, laborers are hired at high wages. Farmers of the capital region, chasing immediate profit, abandon their fields for hire and forsake the essential for the trivial.

sentences.zh: 臣聞一夫不耕，天下有受其饑者，臣竊恐不可。

translations.literal: I have heard that if one man does not plow, there are those under Heaven who suffer hunger because of it. I privately fear this cannot be allowed."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that if one man does not plow, someone under Heaven goes hungry because of it. I fear this cannot be permitted."

sentences.zh: 」帝不應。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not reply.

sentences.zh: 湊又奏曰：「日陽和布氣，萬物生育，土木之間，昆蟲無數。

translations.literal: Cou again submitted: "Now the sun spreads harmonious qi, and the ten thousand things are born and grow. Between earthworks and timber there are countless insects.
translations.idiomatic: Cou submitted again, saying, "The sun now spreads harmonious warmth and the ten thousand things are born and grow. Between earthworks and timber there are countless insects.

sentences.zh: 此時興造，傷殺甚多，臣亦恐非仁聖本旨。

translations.literal: To undertake construction at this time kills and injures very many. I also fear this is not the original intent of benevolent sageliness."
translations.idiomatic: To build at this season kills and injures a great many of them. I also fear this is not the intent of a benevolent sage-ruler."

sentences.zh: 」睿宗方納其言，令在外詳議。

translations.literal: " Only then did Emperor Ruizong accept his words and order detailed discussion outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: " Only then did Emperor Ruizong accept his words and order the matter discussed in detail outside court.

sentences.zh: 中書令崔湜、侍中岑羲謂湊曰：「公敢言此，大是難事。

translations.literal: Chief Minister of the Secretariat Cui Shi and Palace Attendant Cen Yi said to Cou: "Sir, you dared speak thus—this was a very difficult thing."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister of the Secretariat Cui Shi and Palace Attendant Cen Yi said to Cou, "Sir, for you to speak thus was a very bold thing."

sentences.zh: 」湊曰：「叨食厚祿，死且不辭，況在明時，必知不死。

translations.literal: " Cou said: "I enjoy undeserved generous stipend—death I would not refuse. How much more in an enlightened age, where one is sure not to die."
translations.idiomatic: " Cou said, "I enjoy an undeserved generous stipend and would not refuse death. How much more in an enlightened age, where one may be sure not to die."

sentences.zh: 」尋出為陜州刺史，無幾，轉汝州刺史。

translations.literal: " Before long he was sent out as Prefect of Shan and, after not long, transferred to Prefect of Ru.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he was sent out as prefect of Shan, and soon afterward transferred to prefect of Ru.

sentences.zh: 開元二年夏，敕靖陵建碑，征料夫匠。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Kaiyuan an edict ordered a stele erected at Jing Mausoleum and laborers and craftsmen requisitioned.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the second year of Kaiyuan an edict ordered a stele erected at Jing Mausoleum and laborers and craftsmen requisitioned.

sentences.zh: 湊以自古園陵無建碑之禮，又時正旱儉，不可興功，飛表極諫，工役乃止。

translations.literal: Cou held that from antiquity imperial mausoleums had no ritual of erecting steles, and that at the time there was drought and scarcity and construction could not be undertaken. He sent a rapid memorial remonstrating to the utmost, and the labor was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: Cou argued that imperial mausoleums had never had the ritual of erecting steles from antiquity, and that drought and scarcity made construction impossible at the time. He sent an urgent memorial of the strongest protest, and the labor was halted.

sentences.zh: 尋遷岐州剌史。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Prefect of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to prefect of Qi.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為將作大匠。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered court as Grand Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he entered court as Grand Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 時有敕復孝敬廟為義宗，湊上書曰：

translations.literal: At that time there was an edict restoring the Xiaojing Temple as Yizong. Cou submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: At that time an edict restored the Xiaojing Temple under the temple name Yizong. Cou submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 於是敕太常議，遂停義宗之號。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to deliberate, and the title Yizong was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the emperor ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to deliberate, and the title Yizong was dropped.

sentences.zh: 湊前後上書論時政得失，多見采納。

translations.literal: Cou, before and after, submitted memorials discussing the gains and losses of current policy, and many were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Cou submitted memorial after memorial on the strengths and failings of current policy, and many of his recommendations were adopted.

sentences.zh: 再遷河南尹，累封彭城郡公。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Intendant of Henan and was repeatedly enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Intendant of Henan and was enfeoffed as Duke of Pengcheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 以公事左授杭州刺史，轉汾州刺史。

translations.literal: On account of official business he was demoted to the left and appointed Prefect of Hang, then transferred to Prefect of Fen.
translations.idiomatic: On account of an official matter he was demoted to prefect of Hang, then transferred to prefect of Fen.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜太原尹兼節度支度營田大使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Intendant of Taiyuan and concurrently Commissioner for Military Affairs, Finance, and Agricultural Colonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was appointed intendant of Taiyuan and concurrently commissioner for military affairs, finance, and agricultural colonies.

sentences.zh: 其年卒官，年六十五。

translations.literal: That year he died in office at the age of sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died in office at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈幽州都督，謚曰文。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the post of Area Commander of You and a posthumous title of Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed area commander of You and given the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子見素，自有傳。

translations.literal: His son Jiansu has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jiansu has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 湊從子虛心。

translations.literal: Cou's nephew was Xuxin.
translations.idiomatic: Cou had a nephew named Xuxin.

sentences.zh: 湊從子 虛心虛心父維，少習儒業，博涉文史，舉進士。

translations.literal: Cou's nephew Xuxin—Xuxin's father Wei, in youth studied Confucian learning, was broadly versed in literature and history, and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Cou's nephew Xuxin: Xuxin's father Wei studied Confucian learning in his youth, was widely versed in literature and history, and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 自大理丞累至戶部郎中，善於剖判，時員外郎宋之問工於詩，時人以為戶部有二妙。

translations.literal: From Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review he rose through successive posts to Director of the Ministry of Revenue. He was skilled in analysis and judgment. At the time Vice Director Song Zhiwen was accomplished in poetry, and people of the day considered the Ministry of Revenue to have two marvels.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review to director in the Ministry of Revenue and was skilled in legal analysis. At the time Vice Director Song Zhiwen excelled in poetry, and contemporaries said the Ministry of Revenue had two outstanding talents.

sentences.zh: 終於左庶子。

translations.literal: He ended his career as Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 虛心舉孝廉，為官嚴整，累至大理丞、侍御史。

translations.literal: Xuxin was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and served in office with stern rectitude, rising through successive posts to Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, served with stern rectitude, and rose to assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review and attending censor.

sentences.zh: 神龍年，推按大獄，時僕射竇懷貞、侍中劉幽求意欲寬假，虛心堅執法令，有不可奪之志。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong years he investigated a great prison case. At the time the Left Vice Director Dou HuaiZhen and Palace Attendant Liu Youqiu wished to show leniency, but Xuxin firmly upheld the law with a will that could not be swayed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong reign he investigated a major prison case. Vice Director Dou HuaiZhen and Palace Attendant Liu Youqiu wished to show leniency, but Xuxin firmly upheld the law with an unshakable will.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，西域羌胡背叛，時並擒獲，有敕盡欲誅之。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era the Qiang and Hu of the Western Regions rebelled; at the time they were all captured, and there was an edict wishing to execute them all.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong period the Qiang and Hu of the western regions rebelled. When they were captured, an edict ordered that all of them be executed.

sentences.zh: 虛心論奏，但罪元首，其所全者千餘人。

translations.literal: Xuxin submitted a discussion memorial, holding that only the ringleaders should be punished; those he spared numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin submitted a memorial arguing that only the ringleaders should be punished, thereby sparing more than a thousand people.

sentences.zh: 虛心有孝行，及丁父憂，哀毀過禮，鬚鬢盡白，朝廷深所嗟尚。

translations.literal: Xuxin had filial conduct. When he entered mourning for his father, his grief and emaciation exceeded ritual propriety; his beard and temples turned entirely white, and the court deeply admired and commended this.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin was known for filial devotion. When his father died, his grief and emaciation exceeded what ritual required; his beard and temples turned completely white, and the court deeply admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 後遷御史中丞、左右丞、兵部侍郎、荊揚潞長史兼采訪使，所在官吏振肅，威令甚舉，中外以為標準。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Vice Censor-in-Chief, Left and Right Assistant Directors, Vice Minister of War, and Chief Administrator of Jing, Yang, and Lu with concurrent Investigating Commissioner. Wherever he was, officials were stirred to rectitude, his authority and orders were vigorously enforced, and court and countryside took him as a standard.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as vice censor-in-chief, left and right assistant director, vice minister of war, and chief administrator of Jing, Yang, and Lu with concurrent investigating commissioner. Wherever he served, officials were stirred to rectitude and his authority was vigorously enforced; court and countryside alike took him as a standard.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部尚書、東京留守，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Revenue and Defender of the Eastern Capital, then died at the age of sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Revenue and defender of the eastern capital, then died at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 虛心季弟 虛舟季弟虛舟，亦以舉孝廉，自御史累至戶部、司勛、左司郎中，歷荊州長史，洪、魏州刺史兼采訪使，多著能政。

translations.literal: Xuxin's younger brother Xuzhou—Xuzhou, the younger brother, was also recommended as Filial and Incorrupt. From Censor he rose through successive posts to Director in the Ministries of Revenue, Personnel Evaluation, and the Left Department. He served as Chief Administrator of Jing, and as Prefect of Hong and Wei with concurrent Investigating Commissioner, and in many places achieved capable administration.
translations.idiomatic: Xuxin's younger brother Xuzhou was also recommended as Filial and Incorrupt. He rose from censor to director in the ministries of Revenue, Personnel Evaluation, and the Left Department, served as chief administrator of Jing and as prefect of Hong and Wei with concurrent investigating commissioner, and earned a reputation for capable administration.

sentences.zh: 入為刑部侍郎，終大理卿。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of Justice and ended as Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Vice Minister of Justice and ended his career as director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 家有禮則，父子兄弟更踐郎署，時稱「郎官家」。

translations.literal: The family had ritual propriety and rules; father, sons, and brothers in turn filled posts in the Secretariat bureaus, and the age called them "the Bureau-Official Family."
translations.idiomatic: The family observed ritual propriety; father, sons, and brothers in turn held posts in the secretariat bureaus, and contemporaries called them "the Bureau-Official Family."

sentences.zh: 韓思復韓思復，京兆長安人也。

translations.literal: Han Sifu—Han Sifu was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Han Sifu came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖倫，貞觀中為左衛率，賜爵長山縣男。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lun, in the Zhenguan era, was Commander of the Left Guard and was granted the title Baron of Changshan County.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lun served in the Zhenguan era as Commander of the Left Guard and was granted the title Baron of Changshan County.

sentences.zh: 思復少襲祖爵。

translations.literal: Sifu in youth inherited his grandfather's title.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu inherited his grandfather's title in his youth.

sentences.zh: 初為汴州司戶參軍，為政寬恕，不行杖罰。

translations.literal: At first he was Revenue Aide of Bian Prefecture. In governing he was lenient and forgiving and did not impose beating punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as revenue aide of Bian Prefecture, governing with leniency and never imposing corporal punishment.

sentences.zh: 在任丁憂，家貧，鬻薪終喪制。

translations.literal: While in office he entered mourning for a parent. His family was poor, and he sold firewood to complete the mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: While in office he entered mourning for a parent. His family was poor, and he sold firewood to complete the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 時姚崇為夏官侍郎，知政事，深嘉嘆之，擢授司禮博士。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Chong was Vice Minister of the Ministry of Summer Officials and handled government affairs. He deeply praised and sighed over this and promoted him to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chong was then vice minister of the Ministry of War and handling government affairs. He deeply admired Sifu's conduct and promoted him to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 景龍中，累遷給事中。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong era he was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong period he rose to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 時左散騎常侍嚴善思坐譙王重福事下制獄，有司言：「善思昔嘗任汝州刺史，素與重福交遊，召至京師，竟不言其謀逆，唯奏雲『東都有兵氣』。

translations.literal: At that time Left Regular Attendant Yan Shansi was implicated in the affair of Prince Qiao Chongfu and sent to the imperial prison. The responsible offices said: "Shansi formerly served as Prefect of Ru and was on familiar terms with Chongfu. When summoned to the capital he never spoke of Chongfu's plot to rebel, but only submitted that 'there is a martial aura in the eastern capital.'"
translations.idiomatic: At that time Left Regular Attendant Yan Shansi was implicated in the affair of Prince Qiao Chongfu and sent to the imperial prison. The responsible offices argued: "Shansi had once served as prefect of Ru and was on familiar terms with Chongfu. When summoned to the capital he never reported Chongfu's plot to rebel, but only submitted that 'there is a martial aura in the eastern capital.'"

sentences.zh: 據狀正當匿反，請從絞刑。

translations.literal: According to the facts he should properly be charged with concealing rebellion; we request the death penalty by strangulation.
translations.idiomatic: According to the facts he properly concealed rebellion and should be sentenced to strangulation.

sentences.zh: 」思復駁奏曰：「議獄緩死，列聖明規；

translations.literal: " Sifu submitted a rebuttal memorial saying: "To deliberate on prison cases and mitigate death sentences is the enlightened rule of successive sage emperors;
translations.idiomatic: " Sifu submitted a rebuttal memorial, saying, "Deliberating on prison cases and mitigating death sentences is the enlightened rule of successive sage emperors;

sentences.zh: 刑疑從輕，有國常典。

translations.literal: when punishment is doubtful, follow the lighter penalty—this is the standing statute of the state.
translations.idiomatic: when punishment is doubtful, follow the lighter penalty—this is the standing statute of the state.

sentences.zh: 嚴善思往在先朝，屬韋氏擅內，恃寵宮掖，謀危宗社。

translations.literal: Yan Shansi served in the former dynasty when the Wei clan usurped power within the palace, relying on favor in the inner quarters and plotting to endanger the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shansi served in the previous reign when the Wei clan usurped power within the palace, relying on favor in the inner quarters and plotting to endanger the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 善思此時遂能先覺，因詣相府有所發明，進論聖躬必登宸極。

translations.literal: At that time Shansi was able to perceive this in advance, went to the chief minister's residence and made certain disclosures, and advanced the argument that Your Sagely Person must ascend the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shansi perceived the danger in advance, went to the chief minister's residence and made certain disclosures, and argued that Your Majesty must ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 雖交遊重福，蓋謀陷韋氏。

translations.literal: Although he associated with Chongfu, this was in effect a plot to entrap the Wei clan.
translations.idiomatic: Although he associated with Chongfu, this was in effect a plot to entrap the Wei clan.

sentences.zh: 及其謁見，猶不奏聞，將此行藏，即從極法。

translations.literal: When he had an audience he still did not report it. To take this conduct and immediately apply the extreme penalty—
translations.idiomatic: When he had an audience he still did not report the plot. To punish this conduct with the extreme penalty—

sentences.zh: 且敕追善思，書至便發，向懷逆節，寧即奔命？

translations.literal: Moreover, when an edict summoned Shansi, he set out as soon as the letter arrived. If he had harbored rebellious intent, would he have hastened to obey?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when an edict summoned Shansi, he set out as soon as the letter arrived. If he had harbored rebellious intent, would he have hastened to obey?

sentences.zh: 一面疏網，誠合順生；

translations.literal: to loosen the net on one side truly accords with allowing life;
translations.idiomatic: To loosen the net on one side truly accords with sparing life;

sentences.zh: 三驅取禽，來而可宥。

translations.literal: in the three-sided hunt, game that comes forward may be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: in the three-sided hunt, game that comes forward may be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 惟刑是恤，事合昭詳。

translations.literal: To be concerned only with punishment accords with making the matter clear and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: To be concerned only with punishment is to make the matter clear and thorough.

sentences.zh: 請付刑部集群官議定奏裁，以符慎獄。

translations.literal: I request that the case be referred to the Ministry of Justice to gather officials for deliberation, determination, and memorialized decision, in accord with cautious handling of prison cases."
translations.idiomatic: I request that the case be referred to the Ministry of Justice for deliberation by assembled officials and a memorialized decision, in accord with cautious handling of prison cases."

sentences.zh: 」是時議者多雲善思合從原宥，有司仍執前議請誅之。

translations.literal: " At that time many in the deliberations said Shansi ought to be pardoned, but the responsible offices still held to the earlier opinion and requested execution.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time many in the deliberations favored pardoning Shansi, but the responsible offices still held to the earlier opinion and requested execution.

sentences.zh: 思復又駁曰：「臣聞刑人於市，爵人於朝，必僉謀攸同，始行之無惑。

translations.literal: Sifu again submitted a rebuttal saying: "I have heard that punishing a man in the marketplace and ennobling a man in the court must have unanimous counsel in agreement before they are carried out without confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu submitted another rebuttal, saying, "I have heard that punishing a man in the marketplace and ennobling a man at court require unanimous counsel before they are carried out without confusion.

sentences.zh: 謹按諸司所議，嚴善思十才一入，抵罪惟輕。

translations.literal: I respectfully examine what the various offices have deliberated: of ten parts of talent Yan Shansi has one part of guilt; the offense charged admits only the lighter penalty.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully examine what the various offices have deliberated: Yan Shansi is guilty in only one part out of ten; the offense charged admits only the lighter penalty.

sentences.zh: 夫帝閽九重，塗遠千里。

translations.literal: The emperor's gate has nine layers; the road is a thousand li distant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's gate has nine layers; the road to it is a thousand li distant.

sentences.zh: 故借天下之耳以聽，聽無不聰；

translations.literal: Therefore one borrows the ears of all under Heaven to listen, and in listening there is nothing not heard clearly;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore one borrows the ears of all under Heaven to listen, and nothing escapes hearing;

sentences.zh: 借天下之目以視，視無不接。

translations.literal: one borrows the eyes of all under Heaven to see, and in seeing there is nothing not perceived.
translations.idiomatic: one borrows the eyes of all under Heaven to see, and nothing escapes sight.

sentences.zh: 今群言上聞，采擇宜審，若棄多就少，臣實懼焉。

translations.literal: Now many opinions have been reported upward; selection should be careful. If the many are discarded in favor of the few, I truly fear this.
translations.idiomatic: Now many opinions have been reported upward; selection should be careful. If the many are discarded in favor of the few, I truly fear the consequences.

sentences.zh: 輿誦一乖，下情不達，雖欲從眾，其可及乎！

translations.literal: If public report diverges in one point, the feelings below do not reach upward. Even if one wishes to follow the multitude, how can that be attained!
translations.idiomatic: If public report diverges in one point, the feelings below do not reach upward. Even if one wishes to follow the multitude, how can that be achieved!

sentences.zh: 凡百京司，逢時之泰，列官分職，有賢有親。

translations.literal: All the capital offices, meeting a time of great peace, array officials and divide duties—there are the worthy and there are the kin.
translations.idiomatic: All the capital offices, in this time of great peace, array officials and divide duties—there are the worthy and there are the kin.

sentences.zh: 親則列籓諸王，陛下愛子；

translations.literal: The kin are the enfeoffed princes of the imperial house, Your Majesty's beloved sons;
translations.idiomatic: The kin are the enfeoffed princes of the imperial house, Your Majesty's beloved sons;

sentences.zh: 賢則胙茅開國，陛下名臣。

translations.literal: the worthy are those granted fiefs and founding states, Your Majesty's famed ministers.
translations.idiomatic: the worthy are those granted fiefs and founding states, Your Majesty's famed ministers.

sentences.zh: 見無禮於君，寧肯雷同不異？

translations.literal: Seeing lack of propriety toward the ruler, would they willingly echo one another without difference?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing lack of propriety toward the ruler, would they willingly echo one another without dissent?

sentences.zh: 今措詞多出，法令從輕。

translations.literal: Now the wording of many opinions has been produced, and the law should follow the lighter penalty."
translations.idiomatic: Now the wording of many opinions has been produced, and the law should follow the lighter penalty."

sentences.zh: 」上納其奏，竟免善思死，配流靜州。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his memorial and in the end spared Shansi from death, banishing him to Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his memorial and in the end spared Shansi from death, banishing him to Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 思復尋轉中書舍人，數上疏陳得失，多見納用。

translations.literal: Sifu was soon transferred to Secretariat Drafter and repeatedly submitted memorials stating gains and losses; many were adopted and used.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu was soon transferred to Secretariat Drafter and repeatedly submitted memorials on policy; many of his recommendations were adopted.

sentences.zh: 開元初，為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he served as Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign he served as Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 時山東蝗蟲大起，姚崇為中書令，奏遣使分往河南、河北諸道殺蝗蟲而埋之。

translations.literal: At that time locusts rose greatly in the Shandong region. Yao Chong was Chief Minister of the Secretariat and memorialized sending envoys by separate routes to the circuits of Henan and Hebei to kill locusts and bury them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time locusts swarmed across Shandong. Yao Chong was chief minister of the Secretariat and memorialized sending envoys to the circuits of Henan and Hebei to kill locusts and bury them.

sentences.zh: 思復以為蝗蟲是天災，當修德以禳之，恐非人力所能翦滅。

translations.literal: Sifu held that locusts are a heavenly calamity and that one should cultivate virtue to expel them; he feared this was not something human effort could cut down and exterminate.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu held that locusts are a heavenly calamity and that one should cultivate virtue to expel them; he doubted human effort could exterminate them.

sentences.zh: 上疏曰：「臣聞河南、河北蝗蟲，頃日更益繁熾，經歷之處，苗稼都損。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that locusts in Henan and Hebei have in recent days grown still more numerous and fierce; wherever they have passed, seedlings and grain have all been damaged.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial, saying, "I have heard that locusts in Henan and Hebei have grown still more numerous in recent days; wherever they have passed, crops have been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 今漸翾飛河西，遊食至洛，使命來往，不敢昌言，山東數州，甚為惶懼。

translations.literal: Now they gradually fly west of the river, roaming in search of food as far as Luo. Envoys come and go but dare not speak plainly; several prefectures of Shandong are greatly fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Now they are gradually flying west of the river, roaming as far as Luoyang. Envoys come and go but dare not speak plainly; several prefectures of Shandong are greatly fearful.

sentences.zh: 且天災流行，埋瘞難盡。

translations.literal: Moreover, when heavenly calamity spreads, burial is hard to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when heavenly calamity spreads, burial cannot eliminate them all.

sentences.zh: 望陛下悔過責躬，發使宣慰，損不急之務，召至公之人，上下同心，君臣一德，持此誠實，以答休咎。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will repent faults and examine yourself, send envoys to proclaim consolation, reduce non-urgent affairs, summon the most impartial men, unite above and below in one mind, ruler and minister in one virtue, hold to this sincerity, and respond to fortune and misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will repent and examine yourself, send envoys to proclaim consolation, reduce non-urgent affairs, summon the most impartial men, unite ruler and minister in one mind, hold to this sincerity, and respond to fortune and misfortune.

sentences.zh: 前後驅蝗使等，伏望總停。

translations.literal: The former and later locust-driving commissioners—I humbly hope they may all be halted.
translations.idiomatic: The former and later locust-driving commissioners—I humbly hope they may all be halted.

sentences.zh: 《書》云：『皇天無親，惟德是輔；

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'High Heaven has no favorites; it assists only virtue;
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says, 'High Heaven has no favorites; it assists only virtue;

sentences.zh: 人心無親，惟惠是懷。

translations.literal: the hearts of the people have no favorites; they embrace only kindness.'
translations.idiomatic: the hearts of the people have no favorites; they embrace only kindness.'

sentences.zh: 』不可不收攬人心也。

translations.literal: " One cannot fail to gather and win the hearts of the people."
translations.idiomatic: " One cannot fail to win the hearts of the people."

sentences.zh: 」上深然之，出思復疏以付崇。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply approved this and issued Sifu's memorial to give to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor deeply approved this and gave Sifu's memorial to Chong.

sentences.zh: 崇乃請遣思復往山東檢蝗蟲所損之處，及還，具以實奏。

translations.literal: Chong then requested that Sifu be sent to Shandong to inspect places damaged by locusts; when he returned he reported everything in full according to fact.
translations.idiomatic: Chong then requested that Sifu be sent to Shandong to inspect locust damage; when he returned he reported everything according to fact.

sentences.zh: 崇又請令監察御史劉沼重加詳覆，沼希崇旨意，遂箠撻百姓，回改舊狀以奏之。

translations.literal: Chong also requested that Investigating Censor Liu Zhao conduct a further detailed review. Zhao hoped to please Chong's intent, then beat the common people with rods, altered the former reports, and memorialized accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Chong also requested that Investigating Censor Liu Zhao conduct a further detailed review. Zhao hoped to please Chong's intent, beat the common people with rods, altered the former reports, and memorialized accordingly.

sentences.zh: 由是河南數州，竟不得免。

translations.literal: Because of this several prefectures of Henan in the end could not escape disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this several prefectures of Henan in the end could not escape disaster.

sentences.zh: 思復遂為崇所擠，出為德州刺史，轉絳州刺史。

translations.literal: Sifu was then squeezed out by Chong and sent out as Prefect of De, then transferred to Prefect of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu was then forced out by Chong and sent out as prefect of De, then transferred to prefect of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 入為黃門侍郎，加銀青光祿大夫，代裴漼為御史大夫。

translations.literal: He entered court as Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, was given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, and replaced Pei Huan as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate, was granted the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Silver Seal, and replaced Pei Huan as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 思復性恬淡，好玄言，安仁體道，非紀綱之任。

translations.literal: Sifu was by nature tranquil and indifferent, fond of arcane discourse, at ease in benevolence and embodying the Way—not fit for the duties of law and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu was by nature tranquil and indifferent, fond of arcane discourse, at ease in benevolence and embodying the Way—not fit for the duties of law and discipline.

sentences.zh: 無幾，轉太子賓客。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十三年卒，年七十餘。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he died at the age of over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the thirteenth year at the age of over seventy.

sentences.zh: 思復子 朝宗子朝宗，天寶初為京兆尹。

translations.literal: Sifu's son Chaozong—Chaozong, at the beginning of Tianbao served as Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu's son Chaozong served as intendant of Jingzhao at the beginning of the Tianbao reign.

sentences.zh: 思復曾孫 佽曾孫佽，字相之，少有文學，性尚簡淡。

translations.literal: Sifu's great-grandson Ci—Ci, style name Xiangzhi, in youth had literary accomplishment and by nature valued simplicity and detachment.
translations.idiomatic: Sifu's great-grandson Ci, style name Xiangzhi, showed literary talent in his youth and valued simplicity and detachment.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，累辟籓方。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly summoned to regional administrations.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly summoned to regional administrations.

sentences.zh: 自襄州從事征拜殿中侍御史，遷刑部員外。

translations.literal: From aide in Xiang Prefecture he was summoned and appointed Palace Attending Censor, then transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: From aide in Xiang Prefecture he was summoned and appointed palace attending censor, then transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 求為澧州刺史。

translations.literal: He requested appointment as Prefect of Li.
translations.idiomatic: He requested appointment as prefect of Li.

sentences.zh: 歲滿受代，宰相牛僧孺鎮鄂渚，辟為從事，征拜刑部郎中，轉京兆少尹，遷給事中。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was replaced. Chief Minister Niu Sengru was stationed at Ezhu and summoned him as aide; he was then summoned and appointed Director of the Ministry of Justice, transferred to Vice Intendant of Jingzhao, and promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he was replaced. Chief Minister Niu Sengru was stationed at Ezhu and summoned him as aide; he was then summoned as director of the Ministry of Justice, transferred to vice intendant of Jingzhao, and promoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 出為桂州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Observation Commissioner of Gui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as observation commissioner of Gui Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 桂管二十餘郡，州掾而下至邑長三百員，由吏部而補者什一，他皆廉吏量其才而補之。

translations.literal: Gui administration had more than twenty commanderies; from prefectural aides down to district magistrates there were three hundred posts. Those filled through the Ministry of Personnel were one in ten; the rest were all filled by upright officials measuring talent.
translations.idiomatic: Gui administration had more than twenty commanderies; from prefectural aides down to district magistrates there were three hundred posts. Only one in ten was filled through the Ministry of Personnel; the rest were filled by upright officials measuring talent.

sentences.zh: 佽既至桂，吏以常所為官者數百人引謁，一吏執籍而前曰：「具員請補其闕。

translations.literal: When Ci had arrived at Gui, clerks led several hundred men who were customarily made officials to an audience. One clerk came forward holding a register and said: "The posts are filled; please fill the vacancies."
translations.idiomatic: When Ci arrived at Gui, clerks led several hundred men who were customarily made officials to an audience. One clerk came forward holding a register and said, "The posts are filled; please fill the vacancies."

sentences.zh: 」佽戒曰：「在任有政者，不奪所理；

translations.literal: " Ci admonished them, saying: "Those in office who have achieved results in administration shall not be removed from what they govern;
translations.idiomatic: " Ci admonished them, saying, "Those in office who have achieved results shall not be removed from what they govern;

sentences.zh: 有過者，必繩以法。

translations.literal: those who have faults must be bound by law.
translations.idiomatic: those who have faults must be bound by law.

sentences.zh: 缺者當俟稽諸故籍，取其可者，然後補之。

translations.literal: Vacancies should await checking against former registers, taking those who are acceptable, and only then filling them."
translations.idiomatic: Vacancies should await checking against former registers, taking those who are acceptable, and only then filling them."

sentences.zh: 」會春衣使內官至，求賄於郵吏，三豪家因厚其資以求邑宰，佽悉諾之。

translations.literal: " It happened that the Spring-Garments Commissioner arrived from within the palace and sought bribes from postal clerks. Three powerful families therefore increased their funds to seek district magistracies, and Ci assented to all of them.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Spring-Garments Commissioner arrived from the palace and sought bribes from postal clerks, three powerful families increased their funds to seek district magistracies, and Ci assented to all of them.

sentences.zh: 使去，坐以撓法，各笞其背。

translations.literal: When the commissioner left, he charged them with obstructing the law and had each flogged on the back.
translations.idiomatic: When the commissioner left, he charged them with obstructing the law and had each flogged on the back.

sentences.zh: 自是豪猾斂跡，皆得清廉吏以蘇活其人。

translations.literal: From this the powerful and cunning restrained their tracks; all obtained upright officials and thereby revived and sustained the people.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the powerful and cunning restrained themselves; upright officials were appointed and the people were revived.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔置五管都監，計所費盡一境地征，不足飽其意，佽特用儉約處之，遂為定制，君子以為難。

translations.literal: Before long an edict established a general supervisor of the Five Circuits. The calculated expenses exhausted the tax levies of an entire territory and were not enough to satisfy their desires. Ci especially used frugality and restraint in handling this, and it then became a fixed regulation; gentlemen considered this difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict established a general supervisor of the Five Circuits. The calculated expenses exhausted the tax levies of an entire territory and were not enough to satisfy their desires. Ci handled the matter with special frugality, and it then became a fixed regulation; gentlemen considered this a difficult achievement.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，卒於官，贈工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng he died in office and was posthumously given the post of Vice Minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaicheng he died in office and was posthumously appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 張廷珪張廷珪，河南濟源人，其先自常州徙焉。

translations.literal: Zhang Tinggui—Zhang Tinggui was a native of Jiyuan in Henan; his ancestors had moved there from Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tinggui came from Jiyuan in Henan; his ancestors had moved there from Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 廷珪少以文學知名，性慷慨，有誌尚。

translations.literal: Tinggui in youth was famed for literary accomplishment; his nature was generous and he had lofty aims.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui was renowned for literary accomplishment in his youth; he was generous by nature and had lofty aims.

sentences.zh: 弱冠應制舉。

translations.literal: At the capping age he responded to the special examination.
translations.idiomatic: At the capping age he responded to the special examination.

sentences.zh: 長安中，累遷監察御史。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era he was repeatedly promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era he rose to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 則天稅天下僧尼出錢，欲於白司馬阪營建大像。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian taxed monks and nuns throughout the realm to contribute money, wishing to build a great image at the White Horse Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian taxed monks and nuns throughout the realm to contribute money, wishing to build a great image at the White Horse Slope.

sentences.zh: 廷珪上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Tinggui submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui submitted a memorial in protest, saying:

sentences.zh: 則天從其言，即停所作，仍於長生殿召見，深賞慰之。

translations.literal: Empress Zetian followed his words, immediately halted the construction, and still summoned him for audience in the Hall of Long Life, deeply praising and comforting him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zetian followed his advice, immediately halted the construction, and summoned him to audience in the Hall of Long Life, deeply praising and comforting him.

sentences.zh: 景龍末，為中書舍人，再轉洪州都督，仍為江南西道按察使。

translations.literal: At the end of Jinglong he served as Secretariat Drafter, was again transferred to Area Commander of Hong, and still served as Investigating Commissioner of the Jiangnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jinglong era he served as Secretariat Drafter, then as area commander of Hong and investigating commissioner of the Jiangnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 開元初，入為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he entered court as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan reign he entered court as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時久旱，關中饑儉，下制求直諫昌言、弘益政理者。

translations.literal: At that time there had been long drought; Guanzhong suffered famine and scarcity. An edict was issued seeking direct remonstrance, splendid words, and those who would enlarge and benefit government and principle.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a long drought had brought famine to Guanzhong. An edict was issued seeking direct remonstrance and counsel that would enlarge and benefit government.

sentences.zh: 廷珪上疏曰：

translations.literal: Tinggui submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 再遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Vice Minister of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 時監察御史蔣挺以監決杖刑稍輕，敕朝堂杖之，廷珪奏曰：「御史憲司，清望耳目之官，有犯當殺即殺，當流即流，不可決杖。

translations.literal: At that time Investigating Censor Jiang Ting, because the beating punishment at supervised execution was slightly light, was ordered by edict to be beaten in the court hall. Tinggui submitted: "Censors are the law office of clear repute and the eyes and ears of the ruler. If guilty they should be killed if death is fitting, exiled if exile is fitting—they cannot be sentenced to beating.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Investigating Censor Jiang Ting, because the beating punishment at supervised execution was considered too light, was ordered by edict to be beaten in the court hall. Tinggui submitted, "Censors are the law office of clear repute and the eyes and ears of the ruler. If guilty they should be killed if death is fitting, exiled if exile is fitting—they cannot be sentenced to beating.

sentences.zh: 士可殺，不可辱也。

translations.literal: A gentleman may be killed but cannot be humiliated."
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman may be killed but cannot be humiliated."

sentences.zh: 」時制命已行，然議者以廷珪之言為是。

translations.literal: " At the time the ordinance had already been carried out, yet those who discussed the matter held Tinggui's words to be correct.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time the ordinance had already been carried out, yet those who discussed the matter held Tinggui's words to be correct.

sentences.zh: 俄坐泄禁中語，出為沔州刺史，又歷蘇、宋、魏三州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, on account of leaking palace language, he was sent out as Prefect of Mian and then served in succession as Prefect of Su, Song, and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on account of leaking palace secrets, he was sent out as prefect of Mian and then served in succession as prefect of Su, Song, and Wei.

sentences.zh: 入為少府監，加金紫光祿大夫，封范陽男。

translations.literal: He entered court as Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, was given the additional title of Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Gold Seal, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Director of the Court of the Imperial Treasury, was granted the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Brightness with Gold Seal, and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 四遷太子詹事，以老疾致仕。

translations.literal: He was transferred four times to Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then retired on account of age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred four times to Mentor of the Heir Apparent, then retired on account of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 二十二年卒，年七十余，贈工部尚書，謚曰貞穆。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he died at the age of over seventy, was posthumously given the post of Minister of Works, and received the posthumous title Zhenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-second year at the age of over seventy, was posthumously appointed Minister of Works, and given the posthumous title Zhenmu.

sentences.zh: 廷珪素與陳州刺史李邕親善，屢上表薦之，邕所撰碑碣之文，必請廷珪八分書之。

translations.literal: Tinggui had long been on friendly terms with Li Yong, Prefect of Chen, and repeatedly submitted memorials recommending him. For stele texts composed by Yong, he always asked Tinggui to write them in clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui had long been close to Li Yong, prefect of Chen, and repeatedly recommended him in memorials. For every stele text Yong composed, he asked Tinggui to write it in clerical script.

sentences.zh: 廷珪既善楷隸，甚為時人所重。

translations.literal: Tinggui was skilled in regular and clerical script and was greatly valued by people of his time.
translations.idiomatic: Tinggui excelled in regular and clerical script and was greatly esteemed in his day.

sentences.zh: 王求禮王求禮，許州長社人。

translations.literal: Wang Qiuli—Wang Qiuli was a native of Changshe in Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiuli came from Changshe in Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 則天朝為左拾遺，遷監察御史。

translations.literal: In the reign of Empress Zetian he served as Left Reminder and was transferred to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Zetian's reign he served as Left Reminder and was promoted to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 性忠謇敢言，每上封彈事，無所畏避。

translations.literal: By nature he was loyal, forthright, and daring in speech; whenever he submitted sealed impeachments he feared nothing and avoided nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He was loyal, forthright, and fearless in speech; whenever he submitted sealed impeachments he held nothing back.

sentences.zh: 時契丹李盡忠反叛，其將孫萬榮寇陷河北數州，河內王武懿宗擁兵討之，畏懦不敢進。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan Li Jinzhong rebelled; his general Sun Wanrong raided and seized several prefectures of Hebei. Wang Wuyizong of Henei led troops to suppress them but, fearful and timid, dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan Li Jinzhong rebelled, his general Sun Wanrong overran several prefectures in Hebei. Wang Wuyizong of Henei led troops against them but, fearful and timid, dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 既而賊大掠而去，懿宗條奏滄、瀛百姓為賊詿誤者數百家，請誅之。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits plundered on a great scale and departed. Wuyizong submitted an itemized memorial that several hundred households of common people in Cang and Ying had been misled by the bandits and requested their execution.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels plundered heavily and withdrew. Wuyizong submitted an itemized memorial listing several hundred households in Cang and Ying as having been misled by the rebels and requested their execution.

sentences.zh: 求禮執而劾之曰：「此詿誤之人，比無良吏教習，城池又不完固，為賊驅逼，茍徇圖全，豈素有背叛之心哉！

translations.literal: Qiuli seized on this and impeached him, saying: "These people who were misled have lacked good officials to instruct them, and their city walls were not secure. Driven by the bandits, they merely sought to preserve themselves—how could they have harbored rebellion from the first!"
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli seized on this and impeached him, saying, "These misled people lacked good officials to guide them, and their defenses were weak. Driven by the rebels, they merely sought to save themselves—how could they have harbored rebellion from the start!"

sentences.zh: 懿宗擁強兵數十萬，聞賊將至，走保城邑，罪當誅戮。

translations.literal: Wuyizong commanded a strong army of several hundred thousand. When he heard the bandits were coming he fled to defend walled towns—his offense deserves execution.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyizong commanded a strong army of several hundred thousand men. When he heard the rebels were coming he fled to defend walled towns—his offense deserves execution.

sentences.zh: 今乃移禍於詿誤之人，豈是為臣之道？

translations.literal: Now he shifts the disaster onto people who were misled—is this the way of a minister?
translations.idiomatic: Now he shifts the blame onto people who were misled—is this the way of a minister?

sentences.zh: 請斬懿宗以謝河北百姓。

translations.literal: I request that Wuyizong be beheaded to answer to the common people of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: I request that Wuyizong be beheaded to answer to the people of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 」懿宗大懼，則天竟降制赦之。

translations.literal: " Wuyizong was greatly afraid, and Empress Zetian in the end issued an ordinance pardoning him.
translations.idiomatic: " Wuyizong was greatly afraid, and Empress Zetian in the end issued an ordinance pardoning him.

sentences.zh: 契丹陷幽州，饋輓不給，左相豆盧欽望請輟京官兩月俸料以助軍，求禮謂欽望曰：「公祿厚俸優，輟之可也。

translations.literal: The Khitan captured You Prefecture and supply transport failed. Left Chancellor Dou Luqinwang requested suspending two months of salary for capital officials to aid the army. Qiuli said to Qinwang: "Your stipend is generous and your salary ample—suspending it would be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan captured You Prefecture and supply lines failed, Left Chancellor Dou Luqinwang proposed suspending two months of salary for capital officials to aid the army. Qiuli said to Qinwang, "Your stipend is generous and your salary ample—suspending yours would be acceptable.

sentences.zh: 國家富有四海，足以儲軍國之用，何藉貧官薄俸。

translations.literal: The state is rich and possesses the four seas, enough to store supplies for army and state—why rely on the meager salaries of poor officials?
translations.idiomatic: The state is rich and possesses all within the four seas, enough to supply army and state—why rely on the meager salaries of poor officials?

sentences.zh: 公此舉豈宰相法邪？

translations.literal: Is this action of yours the method of a chief minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Is this action of yours worthy of a chief minister?"

sentences.zh: 」欽望作色拒之，乃奏曰：「秦、漢皆有稅算以贍軍，求禮不識大體，妄有訟辭。

translations.literal: " Qinwang changed color and rejected this, then memorialized: "Qin and Han both had tax assessments to support the army. Qiuli does not understand the larger principle and rashly offers disputatious words."
translations.idiomatic: " Qinwang flushed with anger and rejected him, then memorialized, "Qin and Han both levied taxes to support the army. Qiuli does not understand the larger principle and rashly offers disputatious words."

sentences.zh: 」求禮對曰：「秦皇、漢武稅天下，虛中以事邊，奈何使聖朝則效？

translations.literal: " Qiuli replied: "The First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han taxed all under Heaven and emptied the center to serve the frontier—how can you have our sagely dynasty imitate them?
translations.idiomatic: " Qiuli replied, "The First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han taxed all under Heaven and emptied the center to serve the frontier—how can you have our sagely dynasty imitate them?

sentences.zh: 不知欽望此言是大體耶！

translations.literal: Do you not know whether Qinwang's words represent the larger principle!"
translations.idiomatic: Do you not know whether Qinwang's words represent the larger principle!"

sentences.zh: 」事遂不行。

translations.literal: " The matter in the end was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " The proposal was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 時三月雪，鳳閣侍郎蘇味道等以為瑞，草表將賀，求禮止之曰：「宰相調燮陰陽，而致雪降暮春，災也，安得為瑞？

translations.literal: At that time there was snow in the third month. Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion Su Weidao and others took it as an auspicious sign and drafted a memorial to offer congratulations. Qiuli stopped them, saying: "Chief ministers harmonize yin and yang, yet snow falls in late spring—this is a calamity; how can it be an auspicious sign?
translations.idiomatic: When snow fell in the third month, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion Su Weidao and others took it as an auspicious sign and drafted a congratulatory memorial. Qiuli stopped them, saying, "Chief ministers harmonize yin and yang, yet snow falls in late spring—this is a calamity; how can it be an auspicious sign?

sentences.zh: 如三月雪為瑞雪，則臘月雷亦瑞雷也。

translations.literal: If snow in the third month is auspicious snow, then thunder in the twelfth month is also auspicious thunder."
translations.idiomatic: If snow in the third month is auspicious snow, then thunder in the twelfth month is also auspicious thunder."

sentences.zh: 」舉朝嗤笑，以為口實。

translations.literal: " The whole court laughed in scorn and took it as a byword.
translations.idiomatic: " The whole court laughed in scorn and made it a byword.

sentences.zh: 求禮竟以剛正，名位不達而卒。

translations.literal: Qiuli in the end, because of his firm uprightness, died without attaining fame and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Qiuli died without attaining fame or high rank, renowned to the end for his firm uprightness.

sentences.zh: 辛替否辛替否，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Xin Tifou—Xin Tifou was a native of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Tifou came from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 景龍年為左拾遺。

translations.literal: In the Jinglong years he served as Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jinglong period he served as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 時中宗置公主府官屬，安樂公主府所補尤多猥濫。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Zhongzong established staff for princesses' establishments; those appointed to Princess Anle's establishment were especially numerous and lax.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong established staffs for princesses' establishments, appointments to Princess Anle's household were especially numerous and indiscriminate.

sentences.zh: 又駙馬武崇訓死後，棄舊宅別造一宅，侈麗過甚。

translations.literal: Moreover, after the consort Wu Chongxun died, she abandoned the old residence and built another separately, excessively lavish.
