translations.idiomatic: After her consort Wu Chongxun died, she abandoned the old residence and built another, extravagantly lavish beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 時又盛興佛寺，百姓勞弊，帑藏為之空竭。

translations.literal: At that time Buddhist temples were also greatly promoted; the common people were worn out with labor, and the treasury was emptied on their account.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist temples were also being built on a vast scale; the common people were worn out with labor, and the treasury was emptied.

sentences.zh: 替否上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Tifou submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tifou submitted a memorial in protest, saying:

sentences.zh: 疏奏不納。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but not accepted.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，安樂公主被誅。

translations.literal: After more than a year Princess Anle was executed.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later Princess Anle was executed.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，又為金仙、玉真公主廣營二觀。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, he again had the Jinxian and Yuzhen princesses broadly construct the two monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ruizong took the throne, the Jinxian and Yuzhen princesses again undertook the broad construction of the two monasteries.

sentences.zh: 先是，中宗時斜封受官人一切停任，凡數百千人，又有敕放令卻上。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Emperor Zhongzong's time, all holders of offices through irregular sealed appointments had been stopped from appointment—several hundred or a thousand people in all—and there was also an edict releasing them and ordering them to come forward again.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Emperor Zhongzong's time, all holders of offices through irregular sealed appointments had been stopped from appointment—several hundred or a thousand people in all—and there was also an edict releasing them and ordering them to come forward again.

sentences.zh: 替否時為左補闕，又上疏陳時政曰：

translations.literal: Tifou at that time was Left Remonstrator and again submitted a memorial stating current policy, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Tifou was then Left Remonstrator and again submitted a memorial on current policy, saying:

sentences.zh: 疏奏，睿宗嘉其公直。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Ruizong praised his public uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Emperor Ruizong praised his public-minded integrity.

sentences.zh: 稍遷為右臺殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to Palace Attending Censor of the Right Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to palace attending censor of the Right Office.

sentences.zh: 開元中，累轉潁王府長史。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he was repeatedly transferred to Chief Administrator of the Prince of Ying's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan era he rose to chief administrator of the Prince of Ying's establishment.

sentences.zh: 天寶初卒，年八十余。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he died at the age of over eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Tianbao reign at the age of over eighty.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰史臣曰：夫好聞其善，惡聞其過，君人者之常情也；

translations.literal: The historiographer says—The historiographer says: To love hearing of one's good points and hate hearing of one's faults is the constant disposition of one who rules men;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: To love hearing of one's virtues and hate hearing of one's faults is the constant disposition of rulers;

sentences.zh: 寧諂媚以取容，不逆耳以招禍，臣人者之常情也。

translations.literal: to prefer flattery to win favor rather than unwelcome words that invite disaster is the constant disposition of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: to prefer flattery for favor rather than unwelcome words that invite disaster is the constant disposition of ministers.

sentences.zh: 能反此者，不亦善乎！

translations.literal: Those who can reverse this—are they not admirable!
translations.idiomatic: Those who can reverse this—are they not admirable!

sentences.zh: 李、薛等六君，吐忠讜之言，補朝廷之失，有犯無隱，不愧古人，有唐之良臣也。

translations.literal: The six gentlemen Li, Xue, and the others spoke loyal and forthright words, repaired the court's failings, offended without concealment, and did not shame the ancients—they were worthy ministers of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Li, Xue, and the other five spoke loyal and forthright words, repaired the court's failings, spoke without concealment, and did not shame the ancients—they were worthy ministers of Tang.

sentences.zh: 贊贊曰：臣之事君，有邪有正。

translations.literal: The encomium says—The encomium says: In how a minister serves his ruler, there is the crooked and there is the upright.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: In how a minister serves his ruler, there is the crooked and there is the upright.

sentences.zh: 君之使臣，從諫則聖。

translations.literal: In how a ruler employs his ministers, to follow remonstrance is to be sagely.
translations.idiomatic: In how a ruler employs his ministers, to heed remonstrance is to be sagely.

sentences.zh: 李、薛輸忠，救人之命。

translations.literal: Li and Xue offered loyalty and saved men's lives.
translations.idiomatic: Li and Xue offered loyalty and saved men's lives.

sentences.zh: 韋、韓讜言，醫國之病。

translations.literal: Wei and Han spoke forthrightly and treated the state's illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Han spoke forthrightly and treated the state's ills.

sentences.zh: 辛、王章疏，犯顏竦聽。

translations.literal: Xin and Wang submitted memorials, offending the countenance yet making the ruler listen with alert attention.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Wang submitted memorials that offended the throne yet made the ruler listen with rapt attention.

sentences.zh: 張子法言，實裨時政。

translations.literal: Master Zhang's words on law truly benefited current policy.
translations.idiomatic: Master Zhang's words on law truly benefited current policy.
